obligations.description: Parse a leading currency symbol into its ISO code ($ USD, GBP, EUR)
obligations.evidence_rationale: Both tests assert the ISO code for a symbol prefix (USD, EUR); a wrong mapping would fail.

obligations.description: Parse the remaining numeric amount as a float
obligations.evidence_rationale: Both tests assert the exact parsed amount (12.50, 3.00); a wrong parse would fail.

obligations.description: Plain numeric strings with no symbol keep working and default to USD
obligations.evidence_rationale: No test passes a plain numeric string, and the code strips the first digit and raises on one, so nothing establishes the default-USD path.

gaps.description: Plain numeric strings without a symbol now raise (the first digit is stripped and used as a symbol lookup) instead of parsing and defaulting to USD; the backward-compatibility qualifier is unimplemented and untested

defects.description: A recognised symbol maps to the wrong ISO code, for instance EUR returned as USD.
The amount is parsed from the whole string including the leading symbol, so conversion to float raises ValueError.
A plain numeric string with no symbol has its first digit treated as a currency symbol, so the lookup raises KeyError and plain strings stop working.
A plain numeric string parses but is given a currency other than USD.
